<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Add missing autosummary entries for ten legacy deterministic mHC training aliases and nineteen internal low-precision Ulysses primitives. Add the five constructor parameter descriptions to `NVFP4KVMaterializer.__init__`, using the existing class documentation. These cover the 30 actionable findings in the [2026-11-05 documentation report](http://dlswqa-nas:8080/cudnn/flashinfer/flashinfer_document_check_report/flashinfer_v0.7.3_vs_main_8baa822f8_20261105_doc_check_result.html) (internal network).

Render the RMSNorm gradient bound as an RST inline literal so `|dx|` no longer generates an undefined substitution and problematic HTML links. Retain the minimal weight-dtype and prepared LoRA grammar fixes.

The single-head MQA documentation is left to #8374. The report's two path findings are checker false positives: `refs/heads/main` is a Git ref, and `flashinfer/experimental/KERNEL_SOURCES_EXCLUDED.txt` is generated inside release wheels. STALE warnings remain untouched.

Complete the Ulysses section title underline and three KDA section title underlines so they match their title lengths.

## 🚀 Pull Request Checklist

Thank you for contributing to FlashInfer! Before we review your pull request, please make sure the following items are complete.

### ✅ Pre-commit Checks

- [x] I have installed `pre-commit` by running `pip install pre-commit` (or used your preferred method).
- [x] I have installed the hooks with `pre-commit install`.
- [ ] I have run the hooks manually with `pre-commit run --all-files` and fixed any reported issues.

> If you are unsure about how to set up `pre-commit`, see [the pre-commit documentation](https://pre-commit.com/).

## 🧪 Tests

- [ ] Tests have been added or updated as needed.
- [ ] All tests are passing (`unittest`, etc.).
- [ ] This PR requires **full-scope** CI, not targeted tests (expensive; justify below).
      Reason: <!-- e.g. cross-cutting change to shared infrastructure -->

Validation:

- Targeted pre-commit (including mypy/Ruff) and `git diff --check` passed for the constructor documentation change.
- All 29 reported MISSING entries are indexed. The constructor passes the nightly checker's docstring-completeness and five-argument consistency checks.
- `python3 scripts/check_pr_document.py --base origin/main --head HEAD --strict` passed on `6aef2fb22`: 0 new static documentation findings.
- RMSNorm: Docutils rendering previously reproduced the undefined substitution and problematic link at all six source occurrences; all six rendered correctly after the fix.
- No runtime behavior changed; GPU tests were not run. Full Sphinx build is left to Build Docs CI.

- KDA: Docutils confirms the three short-underline warnings are gone; targeted pre-commit passed.
- Across all seven changed Python files, execution AST is unchanged after excluding docstrings and the three documentation-only Notes strings; the remaining edits are RST.

## 🔬 Experimental Track

<!-- Only for PRs submitted under the experimental policy (CONTRIBUTING.md → "Experimental APIs and Backends").
     Leave this section untouched for normal PRs. -->

- [ ] This PR is **experimental**: it adds or changes code under `flashinfer/experimental/` and/or an `@flashinfer_experimental_api`. Tracking issue: #
  - [ ] The tracking issue names an owner, the reason for the experimental path, and a graduation plan with a target release.
  - [ ] Core changes are limited to a thin entry point (signature, shared validation, feature-gate check, backend selection, handoff).
  - [ ] Tests live in `tests/experimental/` and were validated on the intended hardware; a runnable example is included.
  - [ ] Nothing is registered in `flashinfer/aot.py`, and no experimental backend is reachable from `backend="auto"` without `FLASHINFER_ALLOW_EXPERIMENTAL_AUTO_BACKENDS=1`. (Calling an `@flashinfer_experimental_api` or naming a backend explicitly is itself the opt-in and needs no environment variable.)
  - [ ] **Test scope declared below.** The experimental CI lane runs exactly these targets, so keep them as narrow as the change allows.

<!-- Required for experimental PRs. Replace the commented lines below with your targets.
     Do not delete the fence or change its `experimental-tests` tag — the experimental-track
     watcher reads it verbatim to decide which targets to ask CI for. -->

```experimental-tests
# One target per line: a directory or a file. (A pytest ::selector is not
# supported -- the sharding runner cannot consume one.) Must be under
# tests/experimental/ and must exist. Delete these comment lines and add yours, e.g.

#   tests/experimental/my_backend/

```

## Reviewer Notes

The mHC entries document compatibility aliases of `flashinfer.cake_mhc_det_train`, not the experimental selectable-mode implementation. The nineteen Ulysses helpers are decorated for API logging/tracing but live in an internal module and are not exported from `flashinfer.comm`. The index documents their existing role in numerical tests and kernel tooling. Existing prose, API decorators, and STALE entries are preserved.

def _missing_jit_cache_spec_info(spec: JitSpec) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Return report metadata without assuming a particular JIT backend."""
    if isinstance(spec, JitSpecNvcc):

def _set_torch_compile_options():
    import torch._dynamo.config

def _monkeypatch_add_torch_compile(func):
    """
    Replace the given function with its torch.compile version.
    """

    from torch._library.custom_ops import CustomOpDef

    if type(func) is types.FunctionType:
        fn = func
    elif isinstance(func, CustomOpDef):
        fn = func._init_fn
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported fn type {type(func)}")

    fullname = fn.__module__ + "." + fn.__qualname__
    components = fullname.split(".")
    assert components[0] == "flashinfer"
    module = flashinfer
    for component in components[1:-1]:
        module = getattr(module, component)
    if not hasattr(module, components[-1]):
        raise ValueError(f"Failed to monkeypatch: {fullname}")

    def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
        compiled = _TORCH_COMPILE_CACHE.get(fullname)
        if compiled is None:
            # Warmup -- JIT compile / import the kernels.
            #
            # From user side, users also need to warmup the model beforehand,
            # as suggested by PyTorch Cuda Graph docs (not sure if it's also
            # recommended for torch.compile as well.)
            #
            # For the convenience of FlashInfer testing, we do the warmup here,
            # on the first run of the function. The caveat is that the first
            # call will run twice: once to warmup, and another through the
            # compiled version.
            func(*args, **kwargs)

            # Compile
            compiled = torch.compile(
                func,
                fullgraph=True,
                backend="inductor",
                mode="max-autotune-no-cudagraphs",
            )
            _TORCH_COMPILE_CACHE[fn.__name__] = compiled

        return compiled(*args, **kwargs)

    setattr(module, fn.__name__, wrapper)
    print("Applied torch.compile to", fullname)

def pytest_collection_modifyitems(config, items):
    """Skip moe_ep tests on hosts that lack the requisite env / GPUs / arch."""
    nvep_built = False
    try:
        from importlib import import_module

        nvep_built = bool(import_module("flashinfer.moe_ep").available_backends())
    except ImportError:
        pass

    ngpu = torch.cuda.device_count() if torch.cuda.is_available() else 0
    cc = (
        torch.cuda.get_device_capability(0)
        if torch.cuda.is_available() and ngpu > 0
        else (0, 0)
    )

    for item in items:
        if "nvep" in item.keywords and not nvep_built:
            item.add_marker(
                pytest.mark.skip(
                    reason="no moe_ep backend built (EP builds by default; "
                    "check install log for skipped-backend warnings)"
                )
            )
        launched_ranks = int(os.environ.get("WORLD_SIZE", "0"))
        for mk, req in (("gpu_2", 2), ("gpu_4", 4), ("gpu_8", 8)):
            if mk not in item.keywords:
                continue
            if "WORLD_SIZE" not in os.environ:
                # Runners that exist only to run multi-rank tests set this so
                # that a missing launcher fails instead of skipping silently.
                if os.environ.get("FAIL_ON_DISTRIBUTED_SKIP") == "1":
                    raise pytest.UsageError(
                        f"{item.nodeid} needs a torchrun or MPI launch "
                        "(WORLD_SIZE unset)"
                    )
                # Multi-rank tests must be launched via torchrun (see
                # tests/moe_ep/run_tests.sh); under plain pytest auto-discovery
                # (e.g. CI unit-test sweeps) they would hang on dist init.
                item.add_marker(
                    pytest.mark.skip(
                        reason="requires torchrun launch (WORLD_SIZE unset)"
                    )
                )
            elif ngpu < req and launched_ranks < req:
                # An explicit torchrun with WORLD_SIZE >= req overrides the
                # physical GPU count: single-GPU sm_12x boxes (RTX/GB10,
                # DGX-Spark style) run multirank with ranks sharing one GPU

def is_cuda_oom_error_str(e: str) -> bool:
    return "CUDA" in e and "out of memory" in e


def _release_cuda_oom(e: BaseException) -> bool:
    """Return whether ``e`` or a linked exception is a CUDA OOM; if so, free its frames.

    torch.testing.assert_close re-raises an OOM from inside its comparison as a
    RuntimeError caused by the OOM, so both ``__cause__`` and ``__context__`` are
    followed. The skip exception keeps these exceptions alive, and their
    tracebacks would keep the test's frames and GPU tensors allocated into the
    tests that follow.
    """
    chain: list[BaseException] = []
    pending: list[BaseException | None] = [e]
    while pending:
        x = pending.pop()
        if x is None or any(x is seen for seen in chain):
            continue
        chain.append(x)
        pending += [x.__cause__, x.__context__]
    if not any(
        isinstance(x, torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError) or is_cuda_oom_error_str(str(x))
        for x in chain
    ):
        return False
    for x in chain:
        traceback.clear_frames(x.__traceback__)
    return True


@pytest.hookimpl(wrapper=True)
def pytest_runtest_call(item):
    # skip OOM error and missing JIT cache errors
    try:
        yield
    except (torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError, RuntimeError) as e:
        if os.environ.get("FLASHINFER_STRICT_MOE_EP_TESTS") == "1":
            raise
        if _release_cuda_oom(e):
            pytest.skip("Skipping due to OOM")
        elif isinstance(e, MissingJITCacheError):
            # Record the test that was skipped due to missing JIT cache
            test_name = item.nodeid
            spec = e.spec
            module_name = spec.name if spec else "unknown"

            # Create a dict with module info for reporting
            spec_info = _missing_jit_cache_spec_info(spec) if spec else None

            _MISSING_JIT_CACHE_MODULES.add((test_name, module_name, str(spec_info)))
            pytest.skip(f"Skipping due to missing JIT cache for module: {module_name}")
        else:
            raise


def pytest_terminal_summary(terminalreporter, exitstatus, config):
    """Generate JIT cache coverage report at the end of test session"""
    if not _MISSING_JIT_CACHE_MODULES:
        return  # No missing modules

    # If report file is specified, write to file for later aggregation
    # Otherwise, print summary directly
    if _JIT_CACHE_REPORT_FILE:
        from filelock import FileLock

        # Convert set to list for JSON serialization
        data = [
            {"test_name": test_name, "module_name": module_name, "spec_info": spec_info}
            for test_name, module_name, spec_info in _MISSING_JIT_CACHE_MODULES
        ]

        # Use file locking to handle concurrent writes from multiple pytest processes
        Path(_JIT_CACHE_REPORT_FILE).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        lock_file = _JIT_CACHE_REPORT_FILE + ".lock"
        with FileLock(lock_file), open(_JIT_CACHE_REPORT_FILE, "a") as f:
            for entry in data:
                f.write(json.dumps(entry) + "\n")
        return

    # Single pytest run - print summary directly
    terminalreporter.section("flashinfer-jit-cache Package Coverage Report")
    terminalreporter.write_line("")
    terminalreporter.write_line(
        "This report shows the coverage of the flashinfer-jit-cache package."
    )
    terminalreporter.write_line(
        "Tests are skipped when required modules are not found in the installed JIT cache."
    )
    terminalreporter.write_line("")
    terminalreporter.write_line(
        f"⚠️  {len(_MISSING_JIT_CACHE_MODULES)} test(s) skipped due to missing JIT cache modules:"
    )
    terminalreporter.write_line("")

    # Group by module name
    module_to_tests = {}
    for test_name, module_name, spec_info in _MISSING_JIT_CACHE_MODULES:
        if module_name not in module_to_tests:
            module_to_tests[module_name] = {"tests": [], "spec_info": spec_info}
        module_to_tests[module_name]["tests"].append(test_name)

    for module_name in sorted(module_to_tests.keys()):
        info = module_to_tests[module_name]
        terminalreporter.write_line(f"Module: {module_name}")
        terminalreporter.write_line(f"  Spec: {info['spec_info']}")
        terminalreporter.write_line(f"  Affected tests ({len(info['tests'])}):")
        for test in sorted(info["tests"]):
            terminalreporter.write_line(f"    - {test}")
        terminalreporter.write_line("")

    terminalreporter.write_line(
        "These tests require JIT compilation but FLASHINFER_DISABLE_JIT=1 was set."
    )
    terminalreporter.write_line(
        "To improve coverage, add the missing modules to the flashinfer-jit-cache build configuration."
    )

.. _apimhc:

flashinfer.mhc
==============

Multi-head residual combination (mHC) kernels used by Agentic-style residual
mixing with a fixed ``HC=4`` sub-head layout.

.. currentmodule:: flashinfer.mhc

.. autosummary::
    :toctree: ../generated

    mhc_post
    mhc_pre_big_fuse
    mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_prenorm

Training mHC (Cake)
-------------------

Four-stream mHC training forward / backward for hidden sizes 4096, 5120 and
7168 on SM100 and SM103 (4096 on SM107); each call takes the hidden size ``H``
from ``X`` ``[T, 4, H]``: the forward mapping, coefficients and collapse
(``forward_prepare``), the residual mixing (``forward_finish``), the branch
gradient and gradient statistics (``backward_prepare``), the single-cast input
gradient with fixed-order FP32 parameter gradients (``backward_finish``),
checkpoint replay (``forward_stats``) and autograd wrappers around the
external branch. The caller holds the workspaces:
``cake_mhc_det_train_forward_workspace_bytes`` / ``cake_mhc_det_train_forward_workspace``
and ``cake_mhc_det_train_backward_workspace_bytes`` /
``cake_mhc_det_train_backward_workspace`` size and allocate a zero-initialized
buffer for one hidden size (``hidden=``, default 4096) that serves the calls of
that hidden size for every token count up to ``T``,
``cake_mhc_det_train_reset_workspace`` returns such a caller-owned buffer to its
first-use state after an interrupted launch or capture, and
``is_cake_mhc_det_train_supported`` reports whether a device (optionally at a given
hidden size) has every exported route.

CUDA graphs: one training iteration -- the direct entry points, or
``cake_mhc_det_train_prepare`` / ``cake_mhc_det_train_finish`` around the external
branch followed by the loss backward, also inside a non-reentrant
``torch.utils.checkpoint`` -- can be captured whole with ``torch.cuda.graph``,
and its replays are bitwise equal to the eager iteration;
``torch.cuda.make_graphed_callables`` of such a layer works as well. Warm up
before the capture: run the iteration a few times eagerly on a side stream, so
that every kernel is built and loaded and the per-device default workspaces
exist before the capture starts. The launches go to the current stream, so they
follow the capture stream. Use the same workspaces (caller-owned, or the
defaults) for the warm-up, the capture and the replays, at the token count the
graph was captured with. Every launch leaves the ticket words of its workspace
at zero, so a replay needs no host-side reset.
``cake_mhc_det_train_reset_workspace`` restores a caller-owned workspace after an
interrupted launch or capture; callers that need this recovery pass their own
workspaces.

Side streams: ``forward_prepare`` and ``backward_finish`` keep running while a
kernel on another stream holds some SMs, or holds one CTA on every SM that was
launched with a shared-memory carveout preference of at least 50 percent
(``cudaFuncAttributePreferredSharedMemoryCarveout``). With the driver's default
carveout such a side CTA leaves room for at most 1 KB of dynamic shared memory
next to it on its SM, so every launch that needs more waits until the side
kernel's first CTA exits; raise the side kernel's carveout preference to avoid
this. Under a side kernel that holds every SM, ``backward_finish`` still waits
at some token counts up to 4096 on SM100 at hidden 4096, at token counts
1-896, 1921-2112, 2689-2816 and 3585-3648 on SM100 at hidden 5120, at token
counts 1-640 and 961-1024 on SM100 at hidden 7168, at token counts up to 1535
(hidden 5120) and 1151 (hidden 7168) on SM103, and on SM107, which keeps the
static schedule.

.. currentmodule:: flashinfer.cake_mhc_det_train

    :toctree: ../generated

    cake_mhc_det_train_forward_prepare
    cake_mhc_det_train_forward_stats

The model's head, the mean of the last layer's four residual streams, has its
own kernels for hidden sizes 4096, 5120 and 7168 (4096 on SM107):
``cake_mhc_det_train_head_forward`` returns ``Y = X.mean(dim=1)`` bit for bit as
torch computes it for BF16 ``X`` ``[T, 4, H]``,
``cake_mhc_det_train_head_backward`` writes the gradient
``dX[:, i, :] = BF16(dY / 4)`` of each stream or adds it into a caller's

Training mHC with a selectable numerical mode (Cake, experimental)
------------------------------------------------------------------

``flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_mhc_train`` is the same training function
with a ``deterministic: bool = True`` keyword on every entry point except
``cake_mhc_train_finish`` (it follows the package of its handle),
``cake_mhc_train_reset_workspace`` and ``route_key``.

* ``deterministic=True`` (default) runs ``flashinfer.cake_mhc_det_train``
  unchanged, for hidden sizes 4096, 5120 and 7168 (4096 on SM107).
* ``deterministic=False`` runs the non-deterministic package
  ``flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_mhc_train_backend``, for the same hidden
  sizes: 4096, 5120 and 7168 on SM100 / SM103, 4096 on SM107; its entry points
  raise ``ValueError`` for another hidden size. Its backward has no final
  reduction kernel: the column-slab pass adds the ``dfn`` sum of every (column
  slab, token chunk) unit into ``dfn`` with FP32 reductions and folds
  ``dscale`` / ``dbase`` in the same grid.

Numerical contract of ``deterministic=False``: only the summation order of
``dfn`` varies from run to run. Each element lies within ``P`` FP32 roundings
of the fixed-order sum (``P <= 32`` token chunks), and the FP32 reduction
flushes subnormal addends and results to zero. ``dX``, ``dscale``, ``dbase``,
the forward, the statistics replay and ``backward_prepare`` are bitwise the
deterministic values.

Interaction with ``torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)``:

* The entry points of ``flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_mhc_train`` run the
  deterministic package for ``deterministic=False`` and warn once per process
  (``UserWarning``).
* The non-deterministic package never falls back. Its ``backward_finish`` and
  the backward of its prepare node raise PyTorch's alert for an operation
  without a deterministic implementation (``RuntimeError``; with
  ``warn_only=True`` a ``UserWarning``) right before they launch the ``dfn``
  reduction: after their operands pass, and only for ``T > 0``. The prepare
  node alerts also when the mode was enabled between its forward and its
  backward. Its forward,
  statistics, ``backward_prepare`` and workspace entry points do not alert.
* Every compute and workspace entry point of the non-deterministic package
  raises ``ValueError`` unless ``deterministic=False``.

Workspaces: the workspace helpers take the deterministic package's
``hidden=`` keyword (default 4096) in both modes; it accepts the hidden sizes
of the device's architecture. The forward workspace has one layout in both
modes. The ``deterministic=False`` backward workspace is the deterministic one
at the same offsets without the per-chunk FP32 ``dfn`` partials
(``P x 24 x 4H x 4`` bytes at hidden size ``H``), so
``cake_mhc_train_backward_workspace(T, device, hidden=H, deterministic=True)``
serves both modes and ``deterministic=False`` sizes the smaller one. When the
deterministic mode turns a ``deterministic=False`` call with a caller-owned
backward workspace that is too small for the deterministic layout into the
deterministic backward, the call runs on a private zeroed companion buffer of
that workspace, never on the shared default buffer. Inside a CUDA graph
capture a missing companion raises ``ValueError``.

The default workspaces (``workspace=None``) are one buffer per device, hidden
size and power-of-two token-count bucket in each package, shared by every
stream and every graph replay on the device: calls that can run concurrently on
different streams pass caller-owned workspaces. ``deterministic=False`` creates
no default buffer while the current stream of the buffer's device is capturing
a CUDA graph (``ValueError``); warm up with the same ``deterministic`` value,
token count and hidden size before the capture. A companion is allocated
zeroed outside any capture and every completed launch leaves its
ticket words at zero, so it needs no reset; ``cake_mhc_train_reset_workspace``
zeroes the buffer it is given.

The head (``cake_mhc_det_train_head*``) has no cross-token reduction and no
counterpart in this module; use the deterministic names above.

Names: ``flashinfer.cake_mhc_det_train.cake_mhc_det_train_<name>`` ->
``flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_mhc_train.cake_mhc_train_<name>``,
``is_cake_mhc_det_train_supported`` -> ``is_cake_mhc_train_supported`` and
``CakeMHCDetTrain<Node>Function`` -> ``CakeMHCTrain<Node>Function`` (the
non-deterministic package's nodes). The legacy module
``flashinfer.cake_mhc_train`` keeps the same ``cake_mhc_train_*`` names as
aliases of the deterministic objects, without a ``deterministic`` keyword.

Training RMSNorm, opt-in non-deterministic weight gradient (Cake)
-----------------------------------------------------------------

The names the training RMSNorm had before the deterministic package took its

* ``deterministic=True`` runs the deterministic package above and returns its
  bits.
* ``deterministic=False`` runs this package's backward in the form its
  registry lists for each token-count window (the backward's docstring lists
  the windows). In the windows that ship the single-kernel form, one kernel per
  call computes ``dx`` row by row and adds the ``dw`` sums of its CTAs into
  FP64 sums in the workspace, in the order the CTAs finish: ``dw`` is not
  guaranteed bitwise reproducible; ``dx`` is, and it is within one BF16 ulp of
  ``max(|dx|, rms(dx))`` of the deterministic backward's ``dx`` (not always bitwise
  equal to it). In the windows the backward's notes name, a twosum single kernel
  keeps each thread's ``dw`` column sums exact (error-free FP32 products, TwoSum
  compensation) before the FP64 additions, so its ``dw`` error does not grow
  with the token count. The

  fixed-order reduce), rendered into this package. The backward workspace

  counters and FP64 column sums and, for the pair windows, the partial rows.
  Zeroed once, it serves any sequence of ``deterministic=False`` calls it is
  large enough for with no host write: the kernels leave the counters at rest
  and the sums at zero. It serves calls of one mode.

  deterministic package with its own workspace (a caller's ``workspace`` is

  call (``[..., H]`` inputs, an FP32 weight, a width or residual route it does
  not export). The workspace helpers with ``deterministic=False`` warn and
  return the deterministic package's workspace in that mode.

Cake fused BF16 RMSNorm training forward / backward (SM100 / SM103 / SM107)
with a deterministic default and an opt-in non-deterministic weight gradient.

Forward: ``r_t = (mean_j x_tj^2 + eps)^(-1/2)`` in FP32, ``y = BF16((x * r) * w)``.
The only tensor saved for the backward besides the inputs is the FP32 per-row
reciprocal RMS ``rstd`` (``[T]``).  Backward: one fused pass produces
``dx = BF16(r * g * w - x * r^3 * mean(g * w * x))`` and the FP32 weight
gradient ``dw = sum_t g * x * r``.  The optional residual-add fusion computes
``h_new = BF16(h + u)`` first, normalizes ``h_new``, and in the backward adds
the gradient flowing directly through ``h_new`` so that one ``dx`` tensor is
the gradient of both ``h`` and ``u``.

Every entry point takes ``deterministic`` (default ``True``):

* ``deterministic=True`` runs :mod:`flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_det_train` with the
  same arguments: ``dw`` through a fixed row-chunk partition and a fixed-order
  reduction (a main kernel and a reduce kernel), bitwise reproducible for a
  given token count on devices with the same SM count.  The default call
  returns exactly that package's results.
* ``deterministic=False`` runs this package's kernels: the same forward programs
  (the forward has no cross-row reduction) and, per token-count window, the
  backward form this build's registry lists for the window
  (``cake_jit.program_windows``; the backward docstring's notes are generated
  from it).  The single-kernel form, in the windows that ship it: persistent
  CTAs claim row chunks, write ``dx`` and add their per-column ``dw`` sums into
  FP64 sums in the workspace in the order they finish; the CTA that finishes
  last rounds the sums into ``dw``.  ``dx`` is bitwise reproducible and within
  one BF16 ulp of ``max(|dx|, rms(dx))`` of the deterministic backward's ``dx``
  (not always bitwise equal to it); ``dw`` is not guaranteed bitwise
  reproducible (the order of the FP64 additions depends on scheduling).  In
  the windows the backward docstring's notes name, a twosum single kernel keeps
  each thread's ``dw`` column sums exact (error-free FP32 products, TwoSum
  compensation) before the FP64 additions, so its ``dw`` error does not grow
  with ``T``; a kblock single kernel adds the ``dw`` products of each block of
  8 rows in FP32 and keeps the block sums as FP32 TwoSum pairs before
  the FP64 additions, so its ``dw`` error grows slowly with ``T``.  Every other
  window runs
  the deterministic package's backward pair (main kernel and fixed-order
  reduce), rendered into this package.  This path also accepts ``[..., H]`` inputs whose leading dimensions collapse into
  rows (for example a ``[T, heads, 256]`` per-head view sharing one ``w[256]``)
  and an FP32 weight on the routes that ship the FP32-weight programs.
* ``deterministic=False`` while ``torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)`` is
  in effect raises ``RuntimeError``.  With ``warn_only=True`` it warns, the
  forward runs this package's forward programs (deterministic) and the backward
  runs the deterministic package with a workspace of its own; a call that
  package cannot serve (``[..., H]`` inputs, an FP32 weight, a width or residual
  route it does not export) raises one ``RuntimeError`` naming the feature
  instead.  A call that asks for determinism never runs the non-deterministic
  kernels.  ``deterministic`` must be a ``bool`` (``TypeError`` otherwise).

All kernels use FP32 statistics and accumulation (the non-deterministic
single kernel's ``dw`` sums across CTAs in FP64) with IEEE division and square root (no
fast-math).  Inputs and outputs are BF16; ``rstd`` and ``dw``
are FP32.  Row-strided inputs (``x``, ``residual``, ``g``, ``g_residual``)
are accepted when ``stride(1) == 1``, ``stride(0)`` is a multiple of eight
elements and the storage is aligned (32 bytes for the forward inputs, 16 for
the backward); outputs are contiguous.  The token count ``T`` is a runtime
scalar: it may change between calls, ``T == 1`` is supported and ``T == 0``
returns empty outputs (a zero ``dw``) without launching.

The non-deterministic backward's workspace
(``cake_rmsnorm_train_backward_workspace_bytes(T, H, ..., deterministic=False)``
bytes) has one layout, with offsets fixed by the package, for every call: the
deterministic pair's counters, the single kernel's counters and FP64 column
sums (``cake_jit.SUMS_BYTES``, the largest of the package's single kernels)
and, when a window up to ``T`` runs the deterministic pair, its FP32 partial
rows.  Zero the buffer once: after every launch the kernels leave the counters
at rest and the sums at zero, so with no host write one buffer serves any
sequence of ``deterministic=False`` backward calls it is large enough for --
hidden sizes, residual flags, weight dtypes, token counts, windows and CUDA
Graph replays.  A buffer serves calls of one mode: a ``deterministic=True``
call takes the deterministic package's workspace.  Zeroing it again is
harmless.  Give each stream that may run a backward at the same time its own
buffer.  A call with a workspace issues no memset, copy or synchronization; a
call without one allocates and zero-fills one per call (a caching-allocator
call, one fill kernel of about 3 us and about 35 us of host time on B200).
The backward writes all of ``dw``.

Beside kernels resident on other streams (``deterministic=False``): the backward
kernel needs part of its SM's shared memory, registers for its CTA and one CTA
slot, and an SM serves it only once it can switch to that shared-memory
carveout.  A kernel on another stream whose CTAs hold every SM with a small
carveout therefore delays the backward's start until that kernel exits; kernels
that hold only some SMs cost it no more than the SMs they hold.  Setting
``cudaFuncAttributePreferredSharedMemoryCarveout`` to
``cudaSharedmemCarveoutMaxShared`` on such a resident kernel lets the backward
start beside it.  The windows that run the deterministic pair start and wait
exactly as the deterministic backward does, including its whole-SM programs
(see :mod:`flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_det_train`).  A resident kernel that holds a
large dynamic shared-memory allocation on every SM delays the windows whose
programs need more shared memory than it leaves, deterministic-pair windows
included: ``cake_windows.SMEM_WAITS`` and the backward's notes list, per
architecture, route and window, the measured allocation from which the window
waits (``cake_windows.SMEM_SIDE_KB``: the sizes measured).  Programs that need a
whole SM wait beside any kernel resident on every SM, whatever its carveout: the
deterministic package's whole-SM programs where this package runs them -- the
residual-fused hidden 6144 backward in its deterministic-pair windows, and on
R200 (``sm_107a``) the backward of hidden 1536 and 4096 above 1024 tokens and of
hidden 2048 above 256 tokens in deterministic-pair windows (FP32-weight twins
included) and the forward of hidden 6144 above 4096 tokens.
``cake_windows.WHOLE_SM`` and the notes of the forward and backward list them per
architecture, route and token range; no single-kernel window of this package
needs a whole SM at the token counts measured (256 to 16384).  Beside those,
leave some SMs free of the resident kernel.  The forward programs are the
deterministic package's; see :mod:`flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_det_train`.

Usage::

    y, rstd = cake_rmsnorm_train_forward(x, w, eps)
    dx, dw = cake_rmsnorm_train_backward(g, x, w, rstd)                  # deterministic
    dx, dw = cake_rmsnorm_train_backward(g, x, w, rstd, deterministic=False)

    # autograd (dw is returned in w.dtype; the kernels accumulate in FP32)
    y = cake_rmsnorm(x, w, eps)                                          # deterministic
    y = cake_rmsnorm(x, w, eps, deterministic=False)
    y, h_new = cake_rmsnorm(h, w, eps, residual=u, deterministic=False)  # fused add

    # caller-owned non-deterministic workspace (counters, FP64 column sums, partial rows)
    ws = cake_rmsnorm_train_backward_workspace(T, H, x.device, deterministic=False)
    dx, dw = cake_rmsnorm_train_backward(g, x, w, rstd, deterministic=False, workspace=ws)
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import importlib
from typing import Optional

import torch

from . import cake_rmsnorm_train_backend as _backend
from .api_logging import flashinfer_api
from .cake_rmsnorm_train_backend import (  # noqa: F401

        "CakeRMSNormDetFunction",

"""Primitive tests for the general global-grid Ulysses payload path.

Four layers:
1. Structural: grid arithmetic, payload spec, preconditions (no GPU math).
2. Pipeline self-consistency (bit-exact): the packed V section must be
   byte-identical to the standalone V quantizer's output rearranged into the
   destination-major layout, and unpack must reproduce the packed bytes.
3. Numerical: quantized values match a pure-torch reference within the
   quantization step (the kernels compile under --use_fast_math, whose
   division may differ from IEEE torch division by ULPs, so the torch
   reference is a closeness oracle, not a bit oracle).
4. Optional bit-parity against the SageAttention fork reference when the
   package is importable (the authoritative byte gate lives out of tree).
"""

import pytest
import torch

import flashinfer.comm._ulysses_lowp as lowp

requires_sm120 = pytest.mark.skipif(
    not torch.cuda.is_available() or torch.cuda.get_device_capability(0) != (12, 0),
    reason="V2-G requires an SM120 CUDA device",
)

_HEADS = 56
_HEAD_DIM = 128
_SCALE_MAX = 2.25


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Structural
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("local_sequence", "group", "expected_slots"),
    [
        (1, 32, 1),
        (32, 32, 2),
        (50, 32, 3),  # rank 1 spans tokens 50..99 and touches three groups
        (64, 32, 3),
        (64, 64, 2),
        (9440, 32, 296),
        (9440, 64, 149),
    ],
)
def test_slot_upper_bound_formula(local_sequence, group, expected_slots):
    assert lowp.slots(local_sequence, group) == expected_slots
    for world in (2, 4, 8):
        for rank in range(world):
            assert lowp.touched(rank, local_sequence, group) <= lowp.slots(
                local_sequence, group
            )


def test_owner_rule_holds_for_aligned_shapes():
    for world in (2, 4, 8):
        for L in (128, 256, 384, 1152):
            S = world * L
            for group in (32, 64):
                for g in range((S + group - 1) // group):
                    owner = lowp.owner(g, L, group)
                    assert 0 <= owner < world
                    assert (
                        lowp.group_first(owner, L, group)
                        <= g
                        <= lowp.group_last(owner, L, group)
                    )


def test_payload_spec_reference_shape():
    spec = lowp.payload_spec(
        batch_size=1, local_sequence=9440, num_heads=56, head_dim=128, world_size=4
    )
    assert spec["chunk_bytes"] == 50_774_400
    assert spec["payload_bytes"] == 203_097_600
    assert spec["chunk_bytes"] % 128 == 0
    assert spec["payload_reduction_pct"] == pytest.approx(49.9754, abs=1e-3)


def test_payload_spec_rejects_bad_world_size_and_heads():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="world_size"):
        lowp.payload_spec(
            batch_size=1, local_sequence=128, num_heads=56, head_dim=128, world_size=3
        )
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="divisible"):
        lowp.payload_spec(
            batch_size=1, local_sequence=128, num_heads=54, head_dim=128, world_size=4
        )


@requires_sm120
def test_unpack_rejects_unaligned_local_sequence():
    recv = torch.zeros((4, 128), dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="ALIGN-128"):
        lowp.unpack_for_sage(
            recv,
            batch_size=1,
            local_sequence=65,
            local_heads=14,
            head_dim=_HEAD_DIM,
            world_size=4,
            aligned=True,
        )


@requires_sm120
def test_capability_and_layout_constants():
    cap = lowp.capability("cuda")
    assert cap["compiled_q_group"] == lowp.Q_GROUP
    assert cap["compiled_k_group"] == lowp.K_GROUP
    assert cap["compiled_head_dim"] == lowp.HEAD_DIM
    assert cap["supported"] is True
    assert lowp.ALIGNED == "aligned"  # STATS_PROTOCOL renamed


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Shared pipeline driver (single-GPU simulation of all P ranks)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _global_inputs(dtype, world, L, seed=20260902):
    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    q = torch.randn((1, world * L, _HEADS, _HEAD_DIM), device="cuda", dtype=dtype)
    return q, torch.randn_like(q), torch.randn_like(q)


def _stats(k, v, world, L):
    S = world * L
    k_sum = torch.zeros((1, _HEADS, _HEAD_DIM), dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda")
    v_amax = torch.zeros_like(k_sum)
    for r in range(world):
        s = slice(r * L, (r + 1) * L)
        ks, va = lowp.k_sum_v_amax(k[:, s].contiguous(), v[:, s].contiguous())
        k_sum += ks
        v_amax = torch.maximum(v_amax, va)
    return (k_sum / S).to(k.dtype).contiguous(), (v_amax / _SCALE_MAX).contiguous()


def _run_pipeline(q, k, v, k_mean, v_scale, world, L):
    sends = []
    for r in range(world):
        s = slice(r * L, (r + 1) * L)
        q_r, k_r, v_r = (x[:, s].contiguous() for x in (q, k, v))
        q_amax = lowp.q_grouped_amax(q_r, rank=r, world_size=world)
        k_amax = lowp.k_grouped_amax(k_r, k_mean, rank=r, world_size=world)
        sends.append(
            lowp.quant_qkv_pack(
                q_r,
                k_r,
                v_r,
                k_mean,
                q_amax,
                k_amax,
                v_scale,
                rank=r,
                world_size=world,
            )
        )
    return sends


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Pipeline self-consistency (bit-exact within one compiled module)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


@requires_sm120
@pytest.mark.parametrize("world", [2, 4, 8])
@pytest.mark.parametrize("local_sequence", [128, 384])
def test_packed_v_section_matches_standalone_quantizer(world, local_sequence):
    """The payload V section and quant_v_fp8_with_scale share one math path;
    their bytes must agree exactly after the destination-major rearrange."""
    L = local_sequence
    q, k, v = _global_inputs(torch.bfloat16, world, L)
    k_mean, v_scale = _stats(k, v, world, L)
    spec = lowp.payload_spec(
        batch_size=1,
        local_sequence=L,
        num_heads=_HEADS,
        head_dim=_HEAD_DIM,
        world_size=world,
    )
    local_heads = _HEADS // world
    sends = _run_pipeline(q, k, v, k_mean, v_scale, world, L)
    for r in range(world):
        s = slice(r * L, (r + 1) * L)
        v_r = v[:, s].contiguous()
        canonical = lowp.quant_v_fp8_with_scale(v_r, v_scale)  # [1, L, H, D] uint8
        for d in range(world):
            section = sends[r][d][
                int(spec["v_offset"]) : int(spec["v_offset"]) + int(spec["main_bytes"])
            ].view(L, 1, local_heads, _HEAD_DIM)
            heads = slice(d * local_heads, (d + 1) * local_heads)
            expected = canonical[:, :, heads].permute(1, 0, 2, 3)  # [L, 1, h, D]
            assert torch.equal(section, expected.contiguous().view_as(section))


@requires_sm120
@pytest.mark.parametrize("world", [2, 4, 8])
@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", [torch.bfloat16, torch.float16])
def test_unpack_reproduces_packed_bytes(world, dtype):
    """unpack must be a pure rearrangement of the payload bytes: Q/K logical
    tensors and scale tensors must byte-match the corresponding payload
    sections gathered per source."""
    L = 256
    q, k, v = _global_inputs(dtype, world, L)
    k_mean, v_scale = _stats(k, v, world, L)
    spec = lowp.payload_spec(
        batch_size=1,
        local_sequence=L,
        num_heads=_HEADS,
        head_dim=_HEAD_DIM,
        world_size=world,
    )
    local_heads = _HEADS // world
    sends = _run_pipeline(q, k, v, k_mean, v_scale, world, L)
    for d in range(world):
        recv = torch.stack([sends[r][d] for r in range(world)]).contiguous()

    g_first = lowp.group_first(r, L, 32)
    touched = lowp.touched(r, L, 32)
    qf = q_r.float()
    for slot in range(touched):
        g = g_first + slot
        lo = max(g * 32 - r * L, 0)
        hi = min((g + 1) * 32 - r * L, L)
        ref = qf[:, lo:hi].abs().amax(dim=(1, 3)).clamp_(min=1e-7)
        assert torch.equal(q_amax[..., slot], ref), f"q amax slot {slot}"

    send = lowp.quant_qkv_pack(
        q_r,
        k[:, s].contiguous(),
        v[:, s].contiguous(),
        k_mean,
        q_amax,
        k_amax,
        v_scale,
        rank=r,
        world_size=world,

    codes = (
        send[dest, : int(spec["main_bytes"])]
        .view(torch.int8)
        .view(L, 1, local_heads, _HEAD_DIM)
        .permute(1, 0, 2, 3)
        .float()

    heads = slice(dest * local_heads, (dest + 1) * local_heads)

# Smooth-K inputs for the general pipeline's tail and PDL tests

def _smooth_k_inputs(dtype, world, L, used, seed=20260908):
    """Inputs in the regime the K tail repair is actually written for.

    The repair keeps the zero-padded rows of the one mixed group out of that
    group's amax, so it only changes a payload byte when |0 - k_mean| is
    comparable to the live rows' |k - k_mean|.  Plain ``randn`` puts the live
    deviation an order of magnitude ABOVE |k_mean| (measured: 26x), so the
    padded rows never win the max and the repair is a no-op on the bytes --
    which is why a test built on ``randn`` passes with the repair mis-aimed or
    deleted outright.  Large per-channel means with small deviations inverts
    that ratio (measured: padded 13x above live), which is the regime the
    kernel's tail-repair contract describes.
    """
    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    S = world * L
    q = torch.randn((1, S, _HEADS, _HEAD_DIM), device="cuda", dtype=dtype)
    means = torch.randn((1, 1, _HEADS, _HEAD_DIM), device="cuda", dtype=dtype) * 4.0
    k = means.expand(1, S, _HEADS, _HEAD_DIM).contiguous()
    k += torch.randn_like(k) * 1e-3
    v = torch.randn_like(q)
    for x in (q, k, v):
        x[:, used:] = 0
    return q, k, v

def _full_chain(q, k, v, k_mean, v_scale, world, L, used, enable_pdl):
    """Every kernel of the module, launched back-to-back on one stream with no
    host synchronization in between, so the PDL edges really overlap.  A
    misplaced griddepcontrol.wait shows up as a byte difference."""
    outs = []
    sends = []
    for r in range(world):
        s = slice(r * L, (r + 1) * L)
        q_r, k_r, v_r = (x[:, s].contiguous() for x in (q, k, v))
        ks, va = lowp.k_sum_v_amax(k_r, v_r, enable_pdl=enable_pdl)
        qa = lowp.q_grouped_amax(q_r, rank=r, world_size=world, enable_pdl=enable_pdl)
        ka = lowp.k_grouped_amax(
            k_r,
            k_mean,
            rank=r,
            world_size=world,
            used_sequence=used,
            enable_pdl=enable_pdl,
        )
        split = lowp.quant_qkv_pack(
            q_r,
            k_r,
            v_r,
            k_mean,
            qa,
            ka,
            v_scale,
            rank=r,
            world_size=world,
            enable_pdl=enable_pdl,
        )
        v8 = lowp.quant_v_fp8_with_scale(v_r, v_scale, enable_pdl=enable_pdl)
        outs.extend([ks, va, qa, ka, split, v8])
        sends.append(split)
    recv = torch.stack([sends[src][0] for src in range(world)])
    outs.extend(
        lowp.unpack_for_sage(
            recv,
            batch_size=1,
            local_sequence=L,
            local_heads=_HEADS // world,
            head_dim=_HEAD_DIM,
            world_size=world,
            scale_sequence=used,
            enable_pdl=enable_pdl,
        )
    )
    return outs

def _reference_global_stats(k, v, world, L, used, dtype):
    """The production backends' exact reduction: rank-major stack,
    sum(dim=0) / live rows for the mean, amax(dim=0) / 2.25 for V."""
    ks, va = [], []
    for r in range(world):
        s = slice(r * L, (r + 1) * L)
        a, b = lowp.k_sum_v_amax(k[:, s].contiguous(), v[:, s].contiguous())
        ks.append(a)
        va.append(b)
    denom = used if used is not None else world * L
    k_mean = (torch.stack(ks).sum(dim=0) / denom).to(dtype).contiguous()
    v_scale = (torch.stack(va).amax(dim=0) / _SCALE_MAX).contiguous()
    return k_mean, v_scale


def _auto_chain(q, k, v, world, L, used, flatten_gathered=False):
    """local_stats -> simulated AllGather -> finalize_stats -> quant_and_pack
    on every rank; returns (payloads, stats_list)."""
    sends, ctxs = [], []
    for r in range(world):
        s = slice(r * L, (r + 1) * L)
        send, ctx = lowp.local_stats(
            q[:, s].contiguous(),
            k[:, s].contiguous(),
            v[:, s].contiguous(),
            rank=r,
            world_size=world,
            used_sequence=used,
        )
        sends.append(send)
        ctxs.append(ctx)
    gathered = torch.stack(sends).contiguous()
    if flatten_gathered:
        gathered = gathered.view(-1)
    payloads, stats_list = [], []
    for r in range(world):
        s = slice(r * L, (r + 1) * L)
        st = lowp.finalize_stats(gathered, ctxs[r], k[:, s].contiguous())
        payloads.append(
            lowp.quant_and_pack(
                q[:, s].contiguous(), k[:, s].contiguous(), v[:, s].contiguous(), st
            )
        )
        stats_list.append(st)
    return payloads, stats_list


def _reference_protocol2_payloads(q, k, v, world, L, used, k_mean, v_scale):
    """The protocol-2 pipeline composed exactly as the validated sglang
    wiring does it: descriptors and raw-K min/max ride the (simulated)
    AllGather, merge/derive finalize the boundary slots, split pack."""
    q_amaxes, descs, minmaxes = [], [], []
    for r in range(world):
        s = slice(r * L, (r + 1) * L)
        qa = lowp.q_grouped_amax(q[:, s].contiguous(), rank=r, world_size=world)
        descs.append(
            lowp.boundary_descriptors(
                qa, rank=r, local_sequence=L, group=32, world_size=world
            )
        )
        minmaxes.append(
            lowp.k_boundary_minmax(
                k[:, s].contiguous(), rank=r, world_size=world, used_sequence=used
            )
        )
        q_amaxes.append(qa)
    qg = torch.stack(descs).contiguous()
    mmg = torch.stack(minmaxes).contiguous()
    payloads = []
    for r in range(world):
        s = slice(r * L, (r + 1) * L)
        lowp.merge_boundary_amax(
            q_amaxes[r], qg, rank=r, local_sequence=L, group=32, world_size=world
        )
        ka = lowp.k_grouped_amax(
            k[:, s].contiguous(),
            k_mean,
            rank=r,
            world_size=world,
            used_sequence=used,
        )
        lowp.derive_k_boundary_amax(
            ka, mmg, k_mean, rank=r, local_sequence=L, world_size=world
        )
        payloads.append(
            lowp.quant_qkv_pack(
                q[:, s].contiguous(),
                k[:, s].contiguous(),
                v[:, s].contiguous(),
                k_mean,
                q_amaxes[r],
                ka,
                v_scale,
                rank=r,
                world_size=world,
            )
        )
    return payloads
